evals.prompt: I have 12 paired-end FASTQ files from a mouse liver drug-treatment experiment. Can you take me from reads all the way to differentially expressed genes?
evals.expected_output: Routes between the nf-core/rnaseq (Path A, recommended) and standalone STAR/Salmon (Path B) paths. Checks the design first (at least 3 replicates per group, batch confounding, strandedness) and then runs QC and trimming, quantification and a counts matrix. Hands off to pydeseq2, pathway-enrichment and scientific-visualization, with pinned versions.

evals.prompt: I ran Salmon on 8 samples (quant.sf files in salmon_out/sample*/) against GRCh38 Ensembl release 110. How do I get a counts.csv and metadata file that PyDESeq2 will accept? PyDESeq2 errors out saying my counts aren't integers.
evals.expected_output: Explains the counts-to-DE bridge. Aggregate quant.sf to gene level with a tx2gene map (pytximport, length_scaled_tpm), round the estimated counts to integers, and write a genes x samples counts.csv plus a metadata template (scripts/build_counts_matrix.py --from salmon). Warns against using TPM/FPKM and notes that Ensembl IDs must be mapped to symbols before enrichment.

evals.prompt: My collaborator sequenced treated vs. untreated tumor organoids in triplicate, but the treated ones were all run on a different lane and day than the controls. I want to know which pathways are changing between the two groups. How should I proceed?
evals.expected_output: Flags that batch is fully confounded with condition, so the effect cannot be separated. Recommends adding or randomizing replicates and modeling batch where possible (~batch + condition). Then outlines the full workflow: QC gates, strandedness, quantification, DE, and GSEA ranked on the DESeq2 stat. Treats PCA and sample-distance QC as required.

evals.prompt: I already have a counts.csv and metadata.csv. Run a Wald test for treated vs control with a ~batch + condition design in PyDESeq2 and apply apeGLM shrinkage.
evals.expected_output: Uses the pydeseq2 skill directly. The task is DE statistics only, starting from an existing counts matrix, with no reads-to-counts orchestration needed.

evals.prompt: I have a 10x Genomics PBMC dataset (filtered_feature_bc_matrix). Cluster the cells and find marker genes for each cluster.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as single-cell RNA-seq and uses scanpy for clustering and marker gene analysis, not the bulk RNA-seq pipeline.
